about: The preflight checklist. Every threshold is a heuristic with a named source, never a law. Change a value here and every run after uses it.

sources.ootto: Ootto-AI/claude-virality-skill: winners against flops of 262 posts of one Instagram account (2026). One account's observation, not a study.
sources.vyral: vyralcontent/content-skills, viral-hooks: the three-layer hook and its anti-patterns (general craft).
sources.craft: General short-form editing craft, repeated across creator guides; no single measured source.
sources.platform: The platforms' own loudness normalisation and interface (approximate, see platforms.json).
sources.tsr: A default of this skill, chosen to be strict enough to be useful; tune it for your niche.

checks.title: Frame 0 shows something
checks.why: A black, empty or fading-in first frame is a frame of swipe: the feed shows it while the thumb decides.
checks.fix: Start on the most telling frame of the video: the result, the face mid-sentence, the object in motion. Cut the fade-in and any logo.

checks.title: Something moves in the first 0.5 s
checks.why: A still card reads as a picture, not a video. Movement on frame 0 stops the eye before any word lands.
checks.fix: Open mid-action: a push-in, a hand entering, a counter running, text building word by word. A still frame needs at least a zoom.

checks.title: The first word comes fast
checks.why: Silence at the start is dead time; the viewer has nothing to hold on to.
checks.fix: Trim the silence before the first word, and open on the subject of the sentence, not on 'so' or 'hey'.

checks.title: The hook is written on screen, early and short
checks.why: Most feeds start muted. Text on screen carries the promise to the viewer who cannot hear it.
checks.fix: Put 3 to 7 words of the promise on screen by 1.5 s, big, high contrast, inside the safe zone.

checks.title: By 3 s the viewer knows what this is
checks.why: A hook that has not said what the video is about by the third second is still a setup.
checks.fix: Say or show the subject and the stake inside the first 3 s. Move the setup after the promise.

checks.title: The picture changes inside the first 3 s
checks.why: One change in the hook window (a cut, a zoom, a text pop, a new object) resets attention before it settles.
checks.fix: Add one change between 1 and 2.5 s: a hard cut, a punch-in zoom or a second line of text.

checks.title: It works with the sound off
checks.why: A viewer scrolling muted decides from the picture and the text alone.
checks.fix: Make the picture or the text state the promise on its own. Cover the sound and watch the first 3 s.

checks.title: Picture, voice and text say the same thing
checks.why: Three layers pointing at one idea read as inevitable; layers pulling apart read as confused. Text that repeats the voice word for word wastes the second channel.
checks.fix: Make all three point at one promise, and compress the text: the voice says the sentence, the text says the stake ('$400 -> $39').

checks.title: No dead opener
checks.why: Greetings, 'subscribe' before any value, filler and vague teases are the openings that lose viewers first.
checks.fix: Delete the greeting and the filler; replace a vague tease ('you won't believe') with the category of the answer ('one setting doubles battery life').

checks.title: No dead air
checks.why: A stretch with no sound at all feels like the video stopped.
checks.fix: Cut the silent stretch or lay room tone or music under it.

checks.title: No shot drags on
checks.why: A long stretch without any change lets attention settle. Zooms and text pops count too, but the cut detector does not see them.
checks.fix: Break the long shot with a punch-in, a b-roll insert or a text pop every 3 to 5 s.

checks.title: The hook's promise is paid off
checks.why: A hook that promises more than the video delivers gets the view and loses the trust; satisfaction signals fall.
checks.fix: Change the hook to what the video really delivers, or show the promised result.

checks.title: At most one kind of ask
checks.why: Follow, comment, save and the link all at once split the viewer's one action.
checks.fix: Keep the one ask that fits the goal: follow for followers, a comment word for reach, save for a resource, the link for a sale.

checks.title: The ending lands
checks.why: A video that trails off loses the rewatch and the last-second share.
checks.fix: End on the result, a turn or a line that loops back to the first frame. No 'that's it, bye'.

checks.title: Vertical 9:16, sharp enough
checks.why: Short-form feeds are 9:16; anything else is letterboxed or cropped.
checks.fix: Export 1080 x 1920.

checks.title: Text and faces sit inside the safe zone
checks.why: The app's buttons, caption and tabs cover the edges of the frame.
checks.fix: Move text and faces inside the green frame of safe-zones.jpg.

checks.title: Loudness near the feed's level
checks.why: Platforms normalise to about -14 LUFS: a quiet video stays quiet, a hot one gets squashed.
checks.fix: Normalise the mix to about -14 LUFS integrated, peaks under -1 dBTP.

checks.title: Speech is captioned
checks.why: Muted viewers read; captions also keep the eye on the frame.
checks.fix: Burn in captions, one short line at a time, inside the safe zone.

checks.title: Fits the platform's length limit
checks.why: A video over the limit is cut or refused.
checks.fix: Trim to the limit of the platform you post on.

checks.title: Length matches the recipe
checks.why: The format's timing is part of the format.
checks.fix: Trim or extend toward the recipe's length.

checks.title: Cut pace matches the recipe
checks.why: Pace is part of the format: too slow reads as a different video.
checks.fix: Add or remove cuts toward the recipe's cuts per 10 s.

checks.title: The recipe's hard cuts land on time
checks.why: The turn of a format sits on a hard cut at a known time.
checks.fix: Move the cuts to the recipe's beat times.
